description: Hi! I’m a Grade 11 student interested in space, technology, and AI. I have basic Python skills and enjoy solving problems and teamwork. I’m looking for creative, responsible teammates with skills in coding, AI, web design, or science. Beginners are welcome too! Let’s learn together and build an amazing project!
summary:
SURVIVE UNTIL EARTH is an interactive 2D lunar survival and astronaut training game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Designed primarily for students aged 7–12, the game challenges players to survive seven simulated days on the Moon while managing oxygen, water, food, electricity, and equipment failures.

Players explore a lunar base, solve repair minigames, allocate limited spare parts, and make decisions that affect mission resources. The game uses curated historical NASA DONKI space-weather records to introduce educational scenarios involving solar activity and astronaut safety.

Built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, the game offers an interactive tutorial, English and Vietnamese language support, and a mission demonstration mode. Its goal is to make space science and engineering trade-offs more understandable through hands-on decisions.

By connecting scientific information with gameplay consequences, SURVIVE UNTIL EARTH encourages problem-solving, critical thinking, and interest in space exploration.
details:
Project Overview

SURVIVE UNTIL EARTH is a browser-based educational game that simulates the challenges of operating a lunar outpost. Players take the role of a junior astronaut who must survive seven simulated days, maintain essential systems, complete engineering tasks, and prepare for a safe return to Earth.

How It Works

The game connects oxygen, water, electricity, food, temperature, and equipment condition. Players explore the lunar surface, locate malfunctioning facilities, solve interactive repair puzzles, and choose how to use a limited supply of 20 spare-part units.

Equipment failures create difficult decisions. Repairing one system may consume materials needed elsewhere. Players must balance immediate survival with long-term mission objectives.

NASA Science and Data

The game includes scientific references about lunar gravity, extreme temperatures, life-support systems, water recycling, and space radiation.

It also incorporates five curated historical NASA DONKI records or observation groups from May 2024. These records support educational space-weather scenarios in which players consider sheltering, delaying outdoor activities, or reallocating resources.

The historical observations are based on NASA-published information. Resource costs, exposure effects, and other gameplay consequences are simplified educational simulations rather than direct NASA measurements.

Technology

The game was developed using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Canvas. It runs in a web browser without requiring specialized hardware. Qoder and ChatGPT were used to assist with software development, code refinement, and documentation.

Creativity and Educational Value

Instead of presenting space facts only as text, SURVIVE UNTIL EARTH connects scientific concepts to decisions and visible consequences. Its repair minigames, resource dependencies, interactive tutorial, and bilingual interface aim to make space exploration more accessible to young learners.

The intended impact is to encourage critical thinking, problem-solving, and interest in STEM education. The project is an educational prototype; its learning effectiveness has not yet been established through a formal classroom study.
